title: Durably record terminal effect and resource refs for a released attempt
description:
Objective: produce the terminality facts `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` requires and nothing in production currently writes. Second producer repair for task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4, per its rail 1: "if it omits a named fact, repair that producer rather than reconstructing authority here."

MEASURED GAP at HEAD fa39721 across apps/daemon/src (non-test). Four fields of `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` (packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-planning-hold.ts:30,33-34) have NO production producer at all:
- `effectsTerminal` — ZERO hits
- `terminalEffectRefs` — ZERO hits
- `terminalResourceRefs` — ZERO hits
- `resourcesTerminal` — ONE hit, and it is `resourcesTerminalRef` inside apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:200, i.e. a fixture, not a producer.

So a reader asking "were this attempt's effects and resources terminal when it released?" has nothing durable to read. That question cannot be answered from a caller payload without handing an agent the ability to declare its own effects terminal.

WHAT TO COMPOSE RATHER THAN REBUILD: effect terminality already has authority elsewhere — the activation ledger records effect disposition, and `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-kernel.ts` owns `SUPERVISOR_LAYERS`. Resource terminality likewise has scheduler-side authority. This task ENUMERATES what was terminal at release and records the refs durably; it must not re-decide terminality itself. If an effect's or resource's terminal state cannot be read from its own authority, that is UNKNOWN and the attempt is not releasable — never an assumed terminal.

Deliverable: a durable record, written on the same production release path as task-740924b741754955b94a7ccf7fc16bb1, carrying `effectsTerminal`, `resourcesTerminal`, `terminalEffectRefs[]` and `terminalResourceRefs[]` derived from each item's own durable authority.

NOTE THE ENUMERATION SHAPE, and reuse the pattern rather than inventing one: `apps/daemon/src/work/in-flight-attempts.ts` (task-48c0c0db) already establishes how to enumerate durable records bounded and index-backed via `readEventsByTypeAfter`, with ambiguity and decode drift refused rather than skipped. Follow it — an effect silently omitted from `terminalEffectRefs` is an effect nobody proved terminal, which is exactly the false-release this evidence exists to prevent.

NOT in scope: release disposition, lease or slot state (task-740924b7), safe-boundary observation (its own producer task), the evidence reader itself (task-e62e3828), or deciding terminality.

Owned paths: one new module under apps/daemon/src/work/ plus its .js bridge and focused test.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "terminalEffectRefs\|terminalResourceRefs\|effectsTerminal" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v fixtures` returns production producers where all three returned zero.

Each ref is derived from that item's OWN durable authority, not from a caller list: a test supplies a caller-claimed terminal ref for an effect whose durable state is not terminal and asserts the claim is refused or ignored, pinning the exact code and layer.

An effect or resource whose terminal state cannot be READ yields UNKNOWN and blocks release — it is never omitted from the list and never assumed terminal. A test drives an unreadable item and asserts release is not available, with the exact code and layer.

Enumeration is bounded and index-backed via `readEventsByTypeAfter` following the shape of apps/daemon/src/work/in-flight-attempts.ts; a test asserts the read count is proportional to the attempt's own items rather than to total project events, with a literal bound a full-stream walk would fail.
`effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal` are TRUE only when every enumerated item is terminal, and a test with one non-terminal item asserts both the flag is false and the attempt is not releasable.
A mutation that skips an undecodable item instead of refusing turns a NAMED test red — a silently omitted effect is the false-release this record exists to prevent.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately, the test leg prints a nonzero count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: This record ENUMERATES terminality; it never DECIDES it. Each effect's and resource's terminal state comes from its own durable authority — the activation ledger for effects, the scheduler's resource authority for resources.
No caller-supplied terminal ref, terminal flag or item list may become authority. A caller may identify the attempt; it may never supply what was terminal.
Fail closed: an unreadable or undecodable item is UNKNOWN and blocks release. Never skip it — an omitted item is one nobody proved terminal, and the list would then read as complete.
Page with `readEventsByTypeAfter` and follow in-flight-attempts.ts's bounded, index-backed shape; do not walk all project events to filter in memory.
Real SqliteEventStore in tests, closed in a `finally` on every exit path. Target <=250 physical lines; commit only owned paths by explicit pathspec.
